intro: The old clockmaker left everything to whichever apprentice could finish the last clock, and nothing else. It sits on the oak bench with no face and no way to mark the hours, only fourteen narrow drawers that click open like sighs. The apprentices have five stalled movements around the room, each waiting for its answer to be settled before the final works can be wound. Above the bench hangs the will itself, a great ledger whose every line is two numbers: first the bench a piece belongs to, then a place inside that piece. The clockmaker's note says the estate stays locked until someone reads the ledger the way he always read it—each pair as a single instruction, not two facts. No one yet knows what the pairs are asking for, but every apprentice has stopped polishing and started counting.
echo: The oldest clock in the garden is useless after dark and honest all day.

puzzles.title: Moonphase
puzzles.flavor: Every letter here is wearing someone else's coat. The spaces, at least, are honest.

blocks.text: UJ GVD ZHS BIHW NKUF FISNISZI NKIS GVD KHCI HPBIHWG JVDSW NKI HSFMIB MKUZK UF KHSW

puzzles.title: Complication
puzzles.flavor: Fill in the blanks, literally. Some squares have been given to you for free.
hints: A nonogram (paint-by-numbers). The filled picture is the answer written in 5×5 block letters.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Minute Repeater
puzzles.flavor: Confetti, sorted alphabetically by a very tidy intern. Put it back together.
hints: The sentence was cut into three-letter fragments (spaces removed) and alphabetised. Reassemble it using the word lengths; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Mainspring
puzzles.flavor: Samuel would have recognised the rhythm at once, whatever it happened to be wearing.
hints: Morse code: two symbols stand for dot and dash; gaps separate letters.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with M.

puzzles.title: Perpetual Calendar
puzzles.flavor: A board full of noise, and one horseman who knows exactly where to step.

hints: Start on the given square and follow the knight moves; read the letter on each square it lands on.
